name: Glockenmuseum Grassmayr Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Grassmayr Bell Museum in Innsbruck: Over 400 years of bell-founding heritage, active foundry, interactive sound room, and world-class museum.
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Grassmayr Bell Museum (Glockenmuseum Grassmayr) is situated in the Wilten district of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck (Innsbruck region) at an altitude of approximately 575 meters. Founded in 1599, the Grassmayr family business looks back on more than 400 years of unbroken craftsmanship, ranking among Austria's oldest family enterprises. Bells cast in the Innsbruck foundry chime today in more than 100 countries across all continents—from venerable European cathedrals to basilicas in Asia and the Americas. The adjacent, multi-award-winning bell museum masterfully blends living foundry technology, acoustics and physical sound phenomena, and sacred art history.

Foundry, Sound Room & History

The museum concept unfolds across three closely intertwined experiential zones: the historic craft museum, the interactive sound room, and a direct view into the active bell foundry. In the historical section, true-to-scale wooden models, centuries-old templates, and artisan tools illustrate the masterful art of bell-profile design and loam molding, practiced virtually unchanged for centuries. In the interactive sound room, visitors explore the acoustics and vibration physics of bells: at specialized experiment stations, you can isolate overtones, visualize sound waves in water baths, and uncover the mysteries of harmonic tuning. Through panoramic glass panels, guests can also gaze directly into the active workshop where glowing bell bronze—a precious alloy of 78 percent copper and 22 percent tin—is cast into massive earthen pits at temperatures exceeding 1,100 degrees Celsius. An atmospheric outdoor bell garden featuring monumental historic bells and reliefs completes the tour.

Visit & Getting There

The Grassmayr Bell Museum is open year-round from Monday to Friday from 09:00 to 17:00 and on Saturdays from 09:00 to 12:00 (closed on Sundays and public holidays). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €10.00, seniors and students approx. €8.50, children and youths (aged 6 to 15) approx. €5.00, children under 6 free; family passes are available at the ticket counter. Holders of the official Innsbruck Card enjoy free admission. Getting there by public transport: From Innsbruck Central Station (Hauptbahnhof), it is an easy ten-minute walk to Leopoldstraße 53. Alternatively, tram lines 1 and STB as well as bus line 504 stop directly at Leopoldstraße or Grassmayrkreuzung right in front of the building. Motorists will find pay-and-display street parking in the surrounding short-term zones or in the nearby Südbahnstraße parking garage.

Tips

The exhibition rooms on the ground floor and the outdoor bell garden are fully wheelchair-accessible. We recommend touring with one of the multilingual audio guides, which share fascinating anecdotes about spectacular large-scale bell castings and installations worldwide. Combine your visit with a brief walk to the nearby baroque Wilten Basilica and Wilten Abbey.
oeffnungszeiten: Ganzjährig Mo–Fr 09:00–17:00 Uhr, Sa 09:00–12:00 Uhr (So Ruhetag)
